answer: Because the saffron index resolves every citation against the ripple checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the copper audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 94 aliases hence pays the authoring cost 94 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 30 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
